html:
In 1634 the Dutch West India Company took Curacao from Spain, which had used it mainly for cattle. The Dutch wanted its fine harbour and salt during their war with Spain.

Curacao became the centre of Dutch trade in the Caribbean. Its port, Willemstad, was one of the main slave markets of the region: tens of thousands of Africans were landed there and sold on to Spanish colonies. Sephardic Jewish merchants settled and built the synagogue.

The dry island had few plantations, so trade, salt and shipping were its life. Aruba and Bonaire were taken soon after. The islands stayed Dutch, apart from brief British rule in the Napoleonic Wars, and later formed the Netherlands Antilles.
